description:
PR #16 review finding 1: https://github.com/jat10/zaq/pull/16
Reviewed head: 1b2637d9a5284ad7ed3febd9d175288f9dfc6897; base: f736652a1a982bf08e2ac8773f24921329d59d26.

Problem
New widget creation with a non-default live_updates policy can fail when Engine and Channels run on separate nodes. WidgetConnectorSettings.persist/3 inserts with deferred file validation, then persists the changed policy inside the same transaction. LiveUpdateSettings.persist/2 now invokes ChannelConfig.changeset/3, which dispatches a confidential proposal capability event before commit. Bridge.fetch_capability_config/2 reads the proposal ID from storage and rejects a loaded proposal if the row is missing. The Channels connection cannot see the Engine transaction's uncommitted insert. Local same-process dispatch can see it, hiding the regression.

Introduced by this PR: proposal storage checks, persistence-time capability dispatch, and routing policy writes through ChannelConfig.changeset. Previously the policy write used Ecto.Changeset.change/2 and Repo.update/1 within Engine, without this Channels lookup. Normal database isolation is not itself a bug.

Evidence
A temporary independent-connection probe passed while asserting the defect: Bridge.capability_snapshot accepts a loaded uncommitted SMTP proposal on the writer connection but returns {:error, {:channel_not_configured, "email:smtp"}} through Sandbox.unboxed_run on another connection. This proves transaction visibility, not an end-to-end multi-node widget test. Local review artifacts, if still available: /tmp/pr16_boundary_test.exs and /tmp/pr16-boundary.log. Do not depend on temporary files; recreate the regression in the owning test suite.

Agreed implementation direction / Action reuse assessment
Reuse WidgetConnectorSettings transaction and grouped save orchestration, LiveUpdates normalization, ChannelConfig.changeset/FileSettings validation, and the existing confidential NodeRouter/Event capability_snapshot path. For creation, assemble the complete effective proposal including normalized live_updates before inserting. Validate it while the connector is still built, then persist within the existing transaction. Including the final policy in the initial insert should allow the existing policy comparison to avoid a redundant policy write; verify this against actual code before implementing. Preserve the locked existing-connector policy update path. Engine owns authorization, identity and persistence; Channels evaluates capability facts. Do not introduce new Actions, endpoints, bridge callbacks, transaction frameworks, connection sharing, or remove identity checks. Do not merely restore the old policy write and bypass file validation.

Acceptance criteria
- A valid new widget with a non-default streamed-update policy succeeds with capability evaluation using an independent database connection; no uncommitted-row visibility is required.
- Invalid final file settings fail with existing field-error projection, and connector/routing/policy writes roll back atomically.
- Proposed capability facts reflect the final policy and settings, not an intermediate configuration.
- Existing connector locking, lifecycle revision checks, provider/kind/archive identity checks, secret confidentiality, authorization and NodeRouter boundaries remain intact.
- Add a focused regression in the existing widget/persistence suite and reuse current fixtures/assertions. Keep distinct execution-path coverage; avoid new test modules or duplicated infrastructure unless justified.
- Run mix q and isolated relevant suites through Context Mode. Preserve existing expectations; obtain explicit approval if their behavior must change. Follow the parent issue's remaining validation/UX/E2E gates; do not assume this issue authorizes commits, pushes, merges or final precommit previously deferred by the user.

Agent handoff
Read AGENTS.md and applicable docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/code-quality.md, docs/conventions.md, and Channels/Engine service guides. Read module responsibilities before editing. Keep the patch limited to finding 1; other PR review findings are separate work. User requested issue creation only in this turn; no implementation or agent delegation has been performed.
